skills.skill: Orient to the speaker when called
skills.pinpoint: Shows attending to the speaker in any way that works for the learner (turns head or body toward them, pauses activity, looks toward them or the shared item) after the speaker calls for attention; eye contact is not required.

RBT.text: Runs the plan in sessions by cueing, then delivering reinforcement as soon as the learner can orient toward the speaker in whatever form works for the learner, and records data each session.

OT.text: Reviews seating, sensory needs, and hand and body positioning so the learner can attend and hold still comfortably without being forced.

SLP.text: Checks that the learner's hearing and language comprehension support responding to the cue, and suggests a cue (name, sign, or tap on the shoulder) the learner can reliably detect.

GENED.text: Uses the same cue at the start of whole-class directions and acknowledges any attending form that works for the learner.

SPED.text: Builds the cue into classroom routines so that an adult calls the learner by name or signal at the start of snack, then immediately delivers something the learner likes, and shares which times of day go best.

PARA.text: Uses the same cue at arrival, circle, and transitions and reinforces whenever the learner can orient toward the speaker in whatever form works for the learner, noting the settings where it happens.

PSYCH.text: Helps the team interpret avoidance or distress around the cue, and checks that the attending demand fits the learner's arousal level.

CG.text: Practices at home, for example when an adult calls the learner by name or signal at the start of snack, then immediately delivers something the learner likes, and tells the team where the learner does and does not respond.
